the pricing path changed for the CFB one-home-field fix (docs/cfb-calibration/README.md, "One home field"): football/cfb_p4/engine.js reads football/cfb_p4/home_field.js (GENERATED by football/cfb_p4/research/hfa_unify.js, cfb_hfa_unified_v1, promoted) so the rating recursion and every projection use one 2.8-point home field instead of learning 3.2 and projecting 4.082, with the seed ratings rebuilt under it; new projections carry model_version edgedesk_cfb_p4_v1.0.1; football/fbs/build_coverage.js reports the effective version. Walk-forward 2014-2025 (n 8724): spread MAE -0.052 (95% CI -0.082 to -0.021), better in 11 of 12 seasons. Every number published before this row stays exactly as it was shown.

the pricing path changed for the Step 6 audit fixes (audit_report.md sections 8.1 and 9, C1 and C3): football/cfb_p4/engine.js centres the fallback outcome-range distribution (dist.marginDistribution) on the fair margin — the pooled residual PMF has median -1 because it was fitted on a core that projected with a 4.08-point home field, so every card range sat exactly one point below the fair margin — and labels each efficiency feature by its own updates (a feature the play-level feed never supplies says it is the trained seed; absorbed games are counted once per game). No fair margin, total, win probability or cover probability changes: the fair spread, the Normal win probability and the conditioned cover PMF are untouched; only the range quantiles (the terminal, the cards and the slate's p10/p50/p90) and the efficiency labels move, and the app's RESEARCH-labelled player-quality simulator, which reads the same distribution, now centres on the fair margin too. Every number published before this row stays exactly as it was shown.

EDGEDESK CFB WEEK 9 (2026)

Games: 56

Verified major: 0
Investigate: 3
BET decisions: 0 (betting disabled by policy)
Record: —
Primary concern: None beyond ordinary weekly noise.
Research trigger: CALIBRATION_DRIFT

Rolling 4 weeks: MAE 11.972 on 232 games · Season: MAE 12.267 on 291 · Current version: 291 games graded.
One week is never the verdict. No model change follows from this report; research triggers open candidates, promotions need walk-forward evidence.

triggers.question: Is MAE persistently elevated when the quarterback is uncertain or changed?
triggers.threshold: MAE gap > 2 SE, n ≥ 30 in each group

triggers.question: Does EdgeDesk persistently over-project its favourite?
Is there a conference-specific residual bias?
triggers.threshold: a home conference with n ≥ 30 and |mean residual| > 2 SE

triggers.question: Are verified major disagreements failing systematically?
triggers.threshold: n ≥ 20 settled verified and the market moved toward EdgeDesk < 50% of the time

triggers.question: Has probability calibration or interval coverage drifted?
triggers.threshold: last-100 win ECE > 0.06, or 80% coverage outside 75–85%

triggers.question: Has closing-line value deteriorated?
triggers.threshold: last-50 mean CLV < 0 by more than 2 SE, n ≥ 50

triggers.question: Is large rating-state divergence linked to model error (historical walk-forward)?
triggers.threshold: holdout LARGE − LOW MAE difference, and a football-only correction clearing the 0.05 bar

triggers.question: Is the live MAE above the holdout reference?

triggers.rule: A trigger opens research only when its threshold and minimum sample are both met. One ugly game never does. A fired trigger opens a research candidate; it never edits a model.
